title: Ingress-derived-only: the gateway is the only place identity is ever decided

children.title: Agent's own request arrives
lines: carrying whatever identity claim it wants

children.title: STEP 1, Strip every client-supplied identity header, unconditionally
lines: Before any other logic runs. A client-supplied copy of an identity claim is treated as spoofing by definition, it never even reaches a decision.
This is the step most home-grown gateways skip, trusting a header the caller itself set.

children.title: STEP 2, Resolve real identity server-side, from the credential that actually authenticated
lines: Not from anything the client claims. The credential is looked up against a store that distinguishes a human, a workspace, and one specific agent instance.
Each agent instance gets its own row, independently revocable, independently attributable, never shared.

children.title: STEP 3, Re-stamp the identity headers from the VERIFIED row, only now
lines: Every downstream handler reads a workspace/agent identity header, but the value now came from the database row the credential resolved to, never from the client.
One ingress point re-stamps, everywhere else just trusts, no downstream code re-derives identity on its own.

children.title: STEP 4, Deterministic policy decides, outside the model entirely
lines: A policy-as-code engine (Rego, Cedar) evaluates the verified identity against granted capabilities, allow, escalate for approval, or deny. Fail-closed on any error.
